lots.working: No same-item SOLD: none of the Gowans desks is a 1930s to 1940s veneered seven-drawer desk with Huon pine linings. They are later reproductions, other timbers or worn office desks, and they range from $10 to $220, so they are guides only and no maximum is set (keep 0, flip 0). As a guide only, a tidy pedestal desk of this size makes about $110 to $150 hammer in Tasmania ($134.20 to $183 all-in at Armitage's 22%), and a plain one can go for $10 to $45. If the viewing confirms Huon pine linings, a maker's label and a sound chair, it would sit at the top of that guide. Inbound freight $0 (pickup from 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay).

lots.condition: Veneer looks sound with ordinary age wear and no obvious loss or lifting; polish a little dull; glass top loose but apparently intact; drawer interior clean; chair seat clean. Back, underside, runners and chair joints not shown.
lots.question_for_armitage: Is there a Hewett & Inglis label, stamp or any maker's mark on the desk or chair? What is the main timber, and are the drawer linings Huon pine? What are the overall dimensions? Is the glass top included and uncracked, do all seven drawers run freely, and is there a working key? Is the chair sound?

lots.guide_summary: Close entries only (same 1:6 Tumbler model), converted at USD 1 = AUD 1.437 (ECB reference rate, 16/10/2026). 9 SOLD records from the tycocollectors price history, all US, unverified and without listing links: 7 used sales from May to Aug 2023 at US$49.95 to US$165 (A$72 to A$237), all over 24 months old, and 2 brand-new sales at US$400 (A$575) in Dec 2024 and Jan 2025, possibly one listing recorded twice. 5 ASKING eBay listings seen in the site's eBay panel at US$120 to US$339 (A$172 to A$487), not opened. No UNSOLD results. Category guides only, at Gowans: large or boxed Batman car toys $15 to $110 hammer (Oct 2025 to Sep 2026). No Australian sale of this Tumbler was found, and Armitage's own past results could not be searched because the shared WebSearch cap was already used up.
lots.working: No maximum: the only SOLD records inside 24 months (US$400 in Dec 2024 and Jan 2025) are brand new and presumably complete, and the used records (US$49.95 to US$165) are all from 2023, over 24 months old. All are unverified US aggregator records, so none can set a maximum (keep 0, flip 0). As a guide only, a used car with remote made about A$72 to A$237 in 2023, and a car without its remote and battery should be worth well under that, probably about A$40 to A$100. Inbound freight $0 (pickup from 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay).
lots.confidence_reason: No Tyco or Mattel mark is legible, so the identification rests on shape and fittings matching reference photos; completeness is unknown; and the only SOLD evidence is unverified US aggregator records that are either over 24 months old or brand new.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped: (1) SOLD 23/09/2024 US$45.99 'Tyco monster jam 1:6 scale batmobile remote control': a different product, keyword match only. (2) SOLD 16/05/2023 US$99.94 and 28/04/2023 US$85.00: chart-only values with no title or condition, and the same record set demonstrably includes a different product, so the model cannot be confirmed. (3) SOLD Gowans 423164 ($90, 17/07/2026, Batman figure plus a Toy Story style RC buggy): not a Batmobile. (4) ASKING eBay-panel listings at US$59.95 ('Batman Begins Batmobile Tyco RC 2005 Very Good...': scale not stated, could be the smaller 9.6V or 4xAA version tycocollectors warns about), US$24.95 (Monster Jam truck, different product) and US$22.99 (Batmobile M0665, a different, smaller model). Corrected: the Gowans entries now use each lot's own record URL instead of a search URL, with exact sale dates from the auction records; Gowans 369611 is a different set of cars, not a duplicate of 369565. All 10 table rows and the 12 chart values on the tycocollectors page match the researcher's figures.
lots.key_photo_findings: One photo. Black Tumbler body with two round gold buttons on the side, gold nose plates, gold rear suspension arms with springs, raised air-brake flaps, large rear tyres on silver rims and smaller black front wheels: all match the tycocollectors reference photos of the 1:6 G3448 car. Enlarged crops of the nose, side and rear show no Tyco, Mattel or DC marking and no model number. No remote, battery pack or charger in shot. The 68 cm length is from the catalogue and was not checked.
lots.condition: Heavy dust and grime in the recesses, rubbed gold paint on the nose plates, scuffs on body edges; the main parts look present, but small fittings, the underside and the front light cluster cannot be checked from one angle. Untested and probably car only.
lots.question_for_armitage: Does it come with the remote control, the 7.2V battery pack or a charger, or is it the car only? Has it been powered up? Are any parts broken or missing (air-brake flaps, suspension arms, lights)? Is there a Tyco or Mattel marking underneath?

lots.working: Same-item SOLD within 24 months: one, Gowans 365873, a boxed Opemus III at $210 hammer on a single bid (10/10/2025). Keep: $210 / 1.22 = $172.13, rounded down to $170 hammer ($207.40 all-in). Flip: likely resale $210 hammer (the only same-item sale) less an assumed 15% vendor commission ($31.50) and $0 outbound postage (resold through a local auction, buyer collects) = $178.50; / 2.44 = $73.16, rounded down to $70. Inbound freight $0 (pickup from 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay). Caution: both figures rest on one uncontested sale, while loose Opemus and Meopta enlargers made $5 or drew no bids at Gowans in May 2026, so treat $170 as a ceiling, not a target. A flip only works if the $210 result repeats, so this is a keep buy for a darkroom user, not a flip.
